what_this_is: The Workshop row for the use-trillion-from-a-shell folder: the `trillion` command any AI that can run a shell uses to see the person's AIs and their AI jobs, hand and take work, and list and run Workshop tools, with no MCP connection of its own.

payload.label: Use Trillion from any AI's shell: the trillion command (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Let an AI that can run shell commands see my AIs and their jobs, hand and take work, and run my Workshop tools, with no MCP connection of its own
payload.description: The `trillion` command. Every command is ONE call of the engine's one MCP tool (run_resource_operation) at the account's door: the Trillion Mac app's local door when this computer has one, else the public origin. setup signs in once, puts `trillion` on the PATH and writes the skill for each AI app here; whoami, who, publish, send, work, take, finish, fail, stuck, release, withdraw, remove and serve move AI jobs through tools/hand-work-to-ais; tools and call list and run Workshop tools; op runs any engine operation; records replay-from-transcripts brings back the rows this computer's AIs wrote, from their own transcripts (a dry run lists them, --write writes them back in batches and reads a sample back). The credential is the account's existing key or the sign-in login kept, read into memory only, never printed or put on a command line. Every call carries one request key reused on every retry. A copy an owner installed (its install-owner.json marker beside it) is never rewritten by a bare copy, and `trillion update` names who updates it: the command never updates itself.

arguments.description: The trillion command's own arguments, each one word (for example ["who"], ["tools"], ["call", "tool:...", "{...}"]).

output_schema.description: What the command prints; a refusal says which door refused and why, with a non-zero exit code.

needs: the person's own Trillion sign-in (trillion login, or the Mac app's key)
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer from the root of the Workshop checkout. Run `trillion setup` once (it signs in in the browser and puts the command on the PATH), then `trillion help`. Never print or pass the key on a command line. Report what the command printed.
